content:
Hello everyone,

This summer, I wrote a paper (not yet finished) proposing a method for the knapsack problem that is strikingly similar to the one used in "A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling" recently published by OpenAI.

The same wording as been used and the strategy look the same: the use of cutoffs, partitioning or routing by structural classes, compact state representations, preservation of feasible completions, and the establishment of complexity bounds for each structural family.

I already tried to explain here the concept.

My paper is 314 pages and was deposited under a French e-Soleau envelope on July 20, 2026, to establish a dated record of its prior existence.

The method is fully mine, I created all by myself, without AI. I wanted to write a book to generalize the method on every NP problem and link the structural decomposition to number theory but... now the method is already out.

I'm currently working on the version 3 of Lehmer. My plan was to finish ASAP Lehmer and then finish knapsack properly, but I didn't finished in time.

I would appreciate some help. Thank you in advance

ps: I'm using chatGPT for the latex and the python algorithms
This has not really got anything to do with lean as far as I can see so is off-topic for this Zulip.
